data.description:
Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Percoco maintained a Hold rating on Tesla yesterday and set a price target of $400.00.

Andrew Percoco has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors tied to both opportunity and execution risk. He sees meaningful upside in Tesla’s long‑term autonomous trucking opportunity, including attractive economics per Semi and a significant potential revenue and EBIT contribution by 2040. At the same time, these benefits are contingent on Tesla successfully scaling its high-margin autonomous software offerings and achieving the assumed market share in a still-developing segment.

Percoco keeps his base-case price target unchanged at $400 and reiterates an Equal-weight stance, even as the bull case rises to $840 on the back of the enhanced Semi and Network Services outlook. This reflects a view that, while the upside skew is positive, the commercialization timeline, competitive landscape, and regulatory and adoption uncertainties around autonomy justify a Hold rather than a more aggressive rating at present.

data.description:

Stephen Willey has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors tied to Zanza’s regulatory path and Exelixis’s valuation. The FDA’s request for additional Zanza safety and efficacy data, which prompted a major NDA amendment and pushed the PDUFA date to March 3, 2027, introduces timing uncertainty, even though the core outlook for Zanza’s approval in later-line mCRC remains intact.
